back: [[imp:Interest calculated on principal plus any previously earned interest.]]
Each period, interest is added to the balance, and future interest is computed on the new total.
Results in exponential growth over time.

cards.front: How does compound interest differ from simple interest?
back: Simple interest: $$I = P \times R \times T$$, interest constant each period.
Compound interest: $$FV = PV \times (1 + i)^n$$, interest grows because the base grows.
Compound always yields more than simple for the same rate and time.
The total amount accumulated after all compounding periods.
n replaces time in the compound interest formula.
Multiply the beginning balance by (1 + i) for each period.
Or use the formula: $$FV = PV \times (1 + i)^n$$.
cards.front: How do you manually calculate compound amount?
How do you use a future value table?
back: 1. Find n and i for the given compounding frequency.
2. Locate the table factor at intersection of n (row) and i (column).
3. Multiply principal by the factor: $$FV = PV \times \text{Table Factor}$$.
[[imp:The true annual rate of return, accounting for compounding.]]
$$APY = \left(1 + \frac{r}{m}\right)^m - 1$$ where r = nominal rate, m = periods per year.

cards.front: Compare APY for 6% nominal compounded annually vs. semiannually.

back: If compounding was more than annual, APY would be higher than nominal rate.
